land.text: the South Slav lands of Austria-Hungary (Croatia-Slavonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dalmatia, Carniola, Styria, Carinthia) without Istria, Prekmurje and Međimurje, with Syrmia

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Austria-Hungary'. The land is the state's 1918 shape (keyframe 0): the austria-hungary dossier's hand-over (its /ledger/30: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, three Montenegrin cells, minus Istria) less Prekmurje and Međimurje, which were held by Hungary in 1918, plus the Serbian half of Syrmia, which the SHS page counts as part of the state. The austria-hungary dossier hands Prekmurje and Međimurje here and Sremski to serbs (its /ledger/36); that dossier should be aligned. The three Montenegrin cells are that dossier's reading of the Dalmatian coast, not on the SHS page.

land.text: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, joined to Serbia (without Istria, Prekmurje, Međimurje and Syrmia)

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes'. Syrmia went to Serbia on 24 November (ledger), so it is not in this handover; Prekmurje (Yugoslav troops 'took control' on 12 August 1919, Prekmurje page) and Međimurje (joined 9 January 1919, Međimurje County page) were never this state's land and come to the kingdom through the yugoslavia dossier (/ledger/4, 1920/6).

correction.text: the South Slav lands of Austria-Hungary (Croatia-Slavonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dalmatia, Carniola, Styria, Carinthia) without Istria, Prekmurje and Međimurje, with Syrmia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for this state; its Austria-Hungary 1912 outline ends in October 1918 and its Yugoslavia row starts in 1919 at 244,290 km2). The page gives no area ('Estimated population 6,000,000'); the shape resolves to 463 grid cells, about 117,000 km2 (the author's first figure, before this fix, was about 115,000 km2; Cliopatria's Yugoslavia of 1919 adds Serbia, Montenegro, Vojvodina and Macedonia). FIX PASS 1 Nov 2026 after the g-eu-b review. (a) Prekmurje is subtracted (18 municipalities): the Prekmurje page says the region 'was firstly included into the Hungarian Democratic Republic' after the monarchy dissolved and 'On August 12, 1919, Yugoslav troops took control of the region'; the SHS page lists Prekmurje among the Slovene lands the National Council claimed, so it was claimed, not held. The page names Lendava, Hodoš, Dobrovnik, Šalovci, Moravske Toplice, Puconci and Gornji Petrovci and the centres Murska Sobota, Beltinci, Turnišče and Črenšovci, and says there are 19 municipalities without listing them; Cankova, Grad, Kobilje, Kuzma, Odranci, Rogašovci and Velika Polana are the researcher's completion (confidence 2). (b) Međimurje is subtracted: the SHS page says units loyal to the State 'engaged the Hungarian garrison in Međimurje in November 1918' with no outcome; the Međimurje County page has a first attempt defeated at Čakovec, then 'troops commanded by Slavko Kvaternik forced the Hungarian troops to abandon the region' (no month given) and 'On 9 January 1919, Međimurje joined to the newly created Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes'. The contest is a ledger event. (c) Syrmia is added: the SHS page says 'the region of Syrmia, which had become part of the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, seceded' on 24 November, so the Serbian okrug of Srem (Sremski) is in the shape as well as Vukovar-Srijem; it leaves in the 24 November loss. The Italian occupation of 4 November, the loss of Syrmia and the Međimurje contest are ledger events. Confidence 2: the page lists lands, not a frontier. The SHS page's footnote 'Prekmurje annexed by Hungary' sits in the Slovenia row 'Annexed by Italy, Germany, and Hungary' and carries no 1918 date; it is not what the exclusion rests on.

region.text: the South Slav lands of Austria-Hungary (Croatia-Slavonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dalmatia, Carniola, Styria, Carinthia) without Istria, Prekmurje and Međimurje, with Syrmia

ledger.note: 29 October 1918: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is proclaimed at Zagreb. The infobox gives 'Formation: 29 October 1918'; its first president was 'a Slovene, Anton Korošec'; on 19 October the National Council had declared itself 'the supreme representative body of all South-Slavic peoples in the monarchy'. The page lists Croatia-Slavonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dalmatia, Carniola, Styria, Carinthia and Prekmurje; the shape is the austria-hungary dossier's hand-over less Prekmurje and Međimurje (Hungarian-held in 1918) and with Syrmia (see keyframe 0).

region.text: the Italian zone: the Dalmatian coast 'between, and including, the cities of Zadar and Šibenik, with the hinterland extending to Knin and Drniš' (Treaty of Rapallo page), Rijeka, and western Carniola (a 30 km disc at Postojna and the Idrija municipality); the armistice evacuation list is 'Istria, western Carniola, and part of Dalmatia' (Villa Giusti page)

ledger.note: 4 November 1918: Italy occupies the Adriatic coast. The Villa Giusti page: signed 3 November, 'The ceasefire was to start at 15:00 on 4 November', with evacuation of 'Istria, western Carniola, and part of Dalmatia' and no line named in Dalmatia; the SHS page: 'Italian troops then occupied Istria and much of Dalmatia' and 'remained there until 1921, when the Treaty of Rapallo came into effect'. FIX PASS: the region is no longer the whole of Dalmatia (Split and Dubrovnik were never in the Italian zone). The Treaty of Rapallo page (opened 1 Nov 2026) says 'By the end of 1918, the Italian troops occupied Istria and Rijeka, as well as a part of the Dalmatian coast extending between, and including, the cities of Zadar and Šibenik, with the hinterland extending to Knin and Drniš' and 'the northern parts of Dalmatia were the Italian zone', the southern coast being for the United States ('largely confined to Split', the Serbian army holding the rest). It is drawn as the counties Zadarska and Šibensko-Kninska (confidence 2: the counties are wider than the page's coast and hinterland). The Rapallo page adds that Italy 'captured the islands of Hvar, Vis, Korčula, Mljet, Lastovo, and Pag' without dating them; they are not drawn (the gazetteer has no names for them and its cells, about 253 km2, cannot hold them). Western Carniola is named by the armistice but no page gives its line; it is drawn as a 30 km disc at Postojna (14.215 E, 45.775 N, a coordinate because the gazetteer has Postojna only as an admin-1) and the Idrija municipality, the Rapallo page putting the later frontier 'east of Idrija and Postojna'. Rijeka: the Rapallo page says Italian troops occupied it by the end of 1918; the Rijeka page says Croatian troops (79th regiment) mutinied there on 23 October and 'an international force of British, Italian, French and American troops entered the city in November 1918', so its own date is November, not the 4th.

region.text: Međimurje, where units loyal to the State engaged the Hungarian garrison

ledger.note: November 1918: the State's units fight for Međimurje. The SHS page: 'Military units loyal to the State engaged the Hungarian garrison in Međimurje in November 1918' (no outcome given). The Međimurje County page: the National Council sent 'hastily assembled troops' who were defeated at Čakovec; the second attempt, 'troops commanded by Slavko Kvaternik forced the Hungarian troops to abandon the region'. The region is outside the state's 1918 shape (keyframe 0) because the Hungarian garrison held it until after the first fighting. Counterpart hungarian-republic as in yugoslavia/ledger/4.

region.text: Syrmia: 'the region of Syrmia, which had become part of the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, seceded' (Vukovar-Srijem in Croatia and the Serbian okrug of Srem)

ledger.note: 24 November 1918: Syrmia secedes and joins Serbia. The page: 'On 24 November 1918, the region of Syrmia, which had become part of the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, seceded' and joined Serbia; 'Vojvodina then joined the Kingdom of Serbia on 25 November 1918', but Vojvodina is not in this state's shape (the austria-hungary dossier hands it to the Serbs directly). FIX PASS: both halves of Syrmia are drawn, Vukovarsko-Srijemska and the Serbian okrug Sremski, because the page treats Syrmia as one region; confidence is 2 because the page names the region and not the two admin-1 units. Cross-check for other groups: serbs/ledger/28 (1918/11 gain of Sremski) names austria-hungary as counterpart, and austria-hungary/ledger/36 hands Sremski to serbs in October 1918; both should name this slug.

A bridge at the state's end (1 December 1918): the contest passes to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. The Međimurje County page says the Hungarian troops were forced out in 1918 (no month) and 'On 9 January 1919, Međimurje joined to the newly created Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes'; yugoslavia/ledger/4 gains Medimurska from hungarian-republic in June 1920 (Trianon). The page does not date the withdrawal inside this state's life.

region.text: the zone Italy had occupied since the armistice (northern Dalmatia, Rijeka and western Carniola)

ledger.note: 1 December 1918: this record closes with the state, not with the occupation. The SHS page says the Italian troops 'remained there until 1921, when the Treaty of Rapallo came into effect'; the occupation passes to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (the yugoslavia dossier) and is not ended here. The Rapallo page puts the Italian zone in 'the northern parts of Dalmatia' and the 12 November 1920 treaty gave Italy Zadar and the islands Cres, Lošinj, Lastovo and Palagruža; it says nothing of a 1921 withdrawal.

region.text: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, joined to Serbia (without Istria, Prekmurje, Međimurje and Syrmia)

ledger.note: 1 December 1918: the state joins Serbia in the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. 'Dissolution: 1 December 1918 (joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)'; the National Council declared unification on 23-24 November, and on 1 December 'Regent Alexander proclaimed' the unified kingdom. The Croatian Parliament 'never explicitly approved the union with Serbia'. FIX PASS: the handover excludes Prekmurje and Međimurje (never held by the state), Istria and Syrmia (lost 24 November).

wars.name: Italian occupation of the Adriatic coast after the Armistice of Villa Giusti

zones.text: 'Italian troops then occupied Istria and much of Dalmatia and stayed until 1921': drawn as the Italian zone of northern Dalmatia, Rijeka and western Carniola

wars.outcome: Italy occupied Istria and much of Dalmatia under the armistice of 3-4 November 1918 and stayed until 1921; the Treaty of Rapallo ceded Istria to Italy.
wars.note: No fighting is described; the occupation is the armistice's. FIX PASS: the zone is the Rapallo page's Italian zone (Zadar to Šibenik with the hinterland to Knin and Drniš) plus Rijeka and western Carniola, not all of Dalmatia. The Međimurje clash is a separate entry below.

wars.name: Međimurje clash with the Hungarian garrison, November 1918
wars.outcome: The State's units engaged the Hungarian garrison in November 1918; the first attempt was defeated at Čakovec and a second, under Slavko Kvaternik, forced the Hungarian troops out (month not given); Međimurje joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes on 9 January 1919 and Trianon confirmed it in 1920.
wars.note: SHS page: 'Military units loyal to the State engaged the Hungarian garrison in Međimurje in November 1918.' The outcome is from the Međimurje County page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me%C4%91imurje_County).

certainty.note: The state was an unrecognised provisional government; no page gives its frontier, and the Adriatic, Carinthian, Syrmian and Međimurje frontiers were all in dispute. FIX PASS: Lower Styria: the Rudolf Maister page says he 'in the night of 23 November 1918 seized control of the city of Maribor and the surrounding region of Lower Styria', 'secured for the newly formed State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs' (the Slovene National Council for Lower Styria had made him a general on 1 November); his forces joined the Carinthian offensive only in April 1919, after this state ended, and the SHS page lists 'Southern Carinthia and Lower Styria' as disputed. Rijeka: Croatian troops mutinied on 23 October and an international force entered in November 1918 (Rijeka page); the Free State of Fiume page is silent on 1918 dates. Prekmurje and Međimurje were Hungarian-held.

notes: Written 2026-11-01 for batch g-eu-b (2 pages opened; budget 2-5). New dossier: Cliopatria has no row for the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs. THE STATE: the provisional South Slav state at Zagreb, 29 October to 1 December 1918, drawn on the land the austria-hungary dossier hands it (Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, minus Istria). NOT SETTLED: (1) the occupation_end of 1 December closes the record, not the occupation (Italy stayed to 1921 per the page); the yugoslavia dossier has no event for the Italian occupation of Dalmatia and western Carniola 1918-1921, only the 1920 Rapallo loss; a gap-filler should add it; (2) Montenegro: the SHS page says the National Council's 31 October note intended a common state with Serbia and Montenegro; the austria-hungary dossier's three Montenegrin cells are not on this page; (3) Fiume, Međimurje and the Slovene Carinthian and Styrian frontiers (Rudolf Maister at Maribor, Carinthian plebiscite) are not on the pages opened; yugoslavia carries the 1919 contest with republic-of-austria and the Saint-Germain gain; (4) the austria-hungary split event hands Vukovar-Srijem to both this state and serbs; the 24 November loss here resolves it; (5) the Villa Giusti page gives 3 November as the signing and 4 November as the start of the ceasefire; the SHS page says 4 November; (6) wikidata null (not read from a page); (7) the state's own area is not on the page; the region resolves to about 115,000 km2. Counterparts: serbs, kingdom-of-italy, yugoslavia, austria-hungary exist as dossiers or rows. || FIX PASS 1 Nov 2026 after review g-eu-b (7 more pages opened; the Italian occupation of the eastern Adriatic page, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_occupation_of_the_eastern_Adriatic, returned url_not_found). SUPERSEDES (1)-(3) above where they differ. CHANGED: (a) the occupation is the Italian zone (Zadarska, Šibensko-Kninska, Rijeka, western Carniola), not the whole of Dalmatia; (b) the 1918 shape and the handover no longer hold Prekmurje and Međimurje, and hold the Serbian half of Syrmia until the 24 November loss; (c) a Međimurje contest with hungarian-republic (November, bridged to the state's end); (d) wars, sources and certainty updated. NOT SETTLED: the Dalmatian islands the Rapallo page says were captured (undated, no cells); the exact western Carniola line; the Prekmurje municipalities other than the eleven the page names; the Međimurje withdrawal date; Rijeka's own status in November 1918; yugoslavia/ledger/2 still gains Maribor from the Austrian republic on 10 September 1919 although the Maister page has the State holding it from 23 November 1918; serbs/ledger/28 and austria-hungary/ledger/36 disagree with the Syrmia reading here. DISAGREEMENT: the reviewer cites the SHS page's footnote 'Prekmurje annexed by Hungary' as 1918 evidence; the page puts it in the Slovenia row 'Annexed by Italy, Germany, and Hungary' without a date, so it is not used; the exclusion rests on the Prekmurje page. The reviewer's fix subtracts Murska Sobota only; this dossier subtracts 18 municipalities because that municipality is one grid cell and the page counts 19. Gazetteer names needed: admin-1 Tišina (Slovenia), place Postojna, Murska Sobota.
